femoral campanform sensilla encode forces in the TrF joint plane in cockroaches but encode forces in both CTr and TrF joint planes in stick insects.

how the nervous system of insects controls the movements of their legs.
the role of mechanosensory systems in the control of leg movements and how the structure and function of the sense organs are adapted to the biomechanics of leg movements.
how insects use information from their sense organs to control the forces that act upon them and to coordinate the actions of their muscles.

campaniform sense organs that are located in the femur encode forces in the joint planes that are used by muscles for locomotion.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the femoral sensillum in stick insects is more suitable for the control of muscle synergies than that in cockroaches.
in cockroaches, campaniform sensillum on the femur encode forces in a joint plane where forces are not generated by leg muscles.
campaniform sense organs in cockroaches enhance synergies in the TrF joint plane, while those in stick insects enhance synergies in both the TrF and CTr joint planes.

femoral sensilla can contribute to activation synergist groups in both cockroaches and in stick insects.
